newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen weighted, range-bound in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen weighted, range-bound in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is expected to consolidate around Tuesday New York closing levels during Asian trading time on Wednesday, after its extreme topside heaviness was verified by its failure to rise despite the Iraq situation and increasing expectations of a U.S. rate hike, dealers said.
Heavy exporter sales, which emerged in late Tokyo Tuesday, are likely to keep the topside capped near 109.40 yen and prevent the greenback from rising as far as its overnight high.
But in the absence of strong yen buying factors, any losses are likely to be halted by bargain-hunting near 108.80-90 yen, a city bank dealer said.

Dealers said it was hard to determine the impact of Tuesday's military intervention against Iraq without seeing how the situation develops over the next few days, but noted that unless something drastic happens, further dollar bids on this alone are unlikely.

Tuesday's other dollar-supportive factor, an article in the Wall Street Journal that said the Federal Reserve may be mulling a higher-than-expected rise in the Federal Funds rate, saw its positive impact blunted when these increasing rate hike expectations caused sales in stocks and bonds, although prices later recovered to finish higher.
